claims.text: Rofo began in San Francisco in July 2008.
Rofo was started by two former commercial real-estate brokers.
Rofo's early audience was small-business operators seeking commercial space.
The early service aggregated listings from more than 50 sources and had more than 7,800 Bay Area listings by November 2008.
The 2008 coverage described demand among smaller companies for shorter, adaptable leases and documented gaps in the economics of serving small tenants.
By 2010, Rofo was discussing location choice in relation to company character, employees, customers, transportation, peers and room to grow.
Inc. documented Rofo's move from shared space in Potrero Hill to the Financial District and used it to illustrate location tradeoffs.
The 2010 guide discussed Potrero Hill, SoMa and the 2nd Street corridor, as well as Palo Alto and Oakland near Jack London Square, as distinct historical location contexts.
